items.stem: A nurse is preparing to enter the room of a patient with suspected Clostridioides difficile infection and active diarrhea.
items.sourceReferenceTitle: Guideline for Isolation Precautions / Preventing C. diff
items.explanation: Suspected or confirmed C. difficile requires contact precautions. The nurse should put on gown and gloves before room entry.
items.jurisdictionNotes: US infection prevention guidance aligned to CDC standard and transmission-based precautions.
items.rationale: Standard Precautions apply to all patients, and Transmission-Based Precautions are added when indicated. For C. difficile, gown and gloves are essential, and soap and water is preferred for hand cleansing after contact because of spores.
items.leadInQuestion: Which action is the priority before entering the room?

choices.text: Put on a surgical mask
choices.label: A

choices.text: Perform hand hygiene with alcohol-based hand rub only
choices.label: B
C
choices.text: Put on gown and gloves
Ask the patient to wear a mask
choices.label: D

items.scenarioText: The patient has frequent loose stools and requires assistance with hygiene care.

distractorRationale.A: A surgical mask alone does not address the main transmission risk for suspected C. difficile, which requires contact precautions.
distractorRationale.D: Masking the patient is not the priority intervention for active diarrhea and suspected C. difficile.
distractorRationale.B: Alcohol-based hand rub alone is not the preferred method after likely spore exposure.

items.stem: A nurse is caring for a client with neutropenia after chemotherapy.
items.explanation: Fresh flowers and raw produce can increase exposure to organisms for an immunocompromised client.
items.jurisdictionNotes: US oncology nursing infection prevention guidance.
items.rationale: Clients with neutropenia are at high risk for infection, so environmental and dietary precautions reduce preventable exposure to pathogens.
items.leadInQuestion: Which action by the nurse requires correction?
learningObjectives: Apply neutropenic precautions in clinical care

choices.text: Performing hand hygiene before contact
choices.label: A

choices.text: Placing fresh flowers in the room
choices.label: B

choices.text: Monitoring temperature closely
choices.label: C

choices.text: Using dedicated equipment when possible
choices.label: D

items.scenarioText: The client has an absolute neutrophil count of 400/mm3 and reports fatigue.

distractorRationale.A: Hand hygiene is essential to reduce transmission of pathogens to the client.
distractorRationale.C: Fever may be the first sign of infection in neutropenic clients and should be monitored closely.

items.stem: A nurse is preparing to administer medications through a nasogastric tube.
items.explanation: Verifying tube placement before medication administration reduces the risk of aspiration and improper delivery.
items.jurisdictionNotes: US medication safety guidance for enteral routes.
items.rationale: Medication safety requires confirmation that the medication will enter the gastrointestinal tract rather than the respiratory tract.
items.leadInQuestion: Which action is the priority before giving the medications?
learningObjectives: Prioritize safe medication administration through enteral tubes

choices.text: Verify tube placement according to policy
choices.label: A

choices.text: Mix all medications together to save time
choices.label: B

choices.text: Crush enteric-coated tablets if they are difficult to swallow
choices.label: C

choices.text: Add medications directly to the feeding formula bag
choices.label: D

items.scenarioText: The client receives intermittent tube feedings and has several scheduled morning medications.

distractorRationale.B: Mixing medications increases incompatibility and error risk.
distractorRationale.C: Enteric-coated medications should not be crushed because this changes intended drug release.
distractorRationale.D: Medications should not be mixed into feeding bags because dosing and tube patency can be compromised.

items.stem: A nurse is reviewing delegation assignments with an assistive personnel member caring for a client on seizure precautions.
items.explanation: Padding side rails and maintaining a safe environment are appropriate delegated seizure-precaution tasks.
items.jurisdictionNotes: US nursing delegation principles aligned to standard RN accountability.
items.rationale: The RN retains assessment and teaching responsibilities, while routine safety setup tasks may be delegated appropriately.
items.leadInQuestion: Which task is appropriate for the nurse to delegate?
learningObjectives: Differentiate delegable tasks from RN-only responsibilities

choices.text: Teaching the client about aura symptoms
choices.label: A

choices.text: Assessing the client after a seizure episode
choices.label: B

choices.text: Padding the side rails and keeping the bed in low position
choices.label: C

choices.text: Deciding whether an as-needed antiseizure medication is needed
choices.label: D

items.scenarioText: The client has a history of tonic-clonic seizures and was admitted for medication adjustment.

distractorRationale.A: Teaching requires nursing judgment and should be performed by the RN.
distractorRationale.B: Assessment after a seizure is an RN responsibility.
distractorRationale.D: Medication decisions require nursing assessment and provider orders.

items.stem: A nurse is admitting a client with active pulmonary tuberculosis to the unit.
items.explanation: Pulmonary tuberculosis requires airborne precautions and placement in a negative-pressure room.
items.rationale: Airborne diseases require controls that limit spread of droplet nuclei, including a negative-pressure room and fit-tested respirator use.
items.leadInQuestion: Which action should the nurse take first?

choices.text: Place the client in a semi-private room with another respiratory client
choices.label: A

choices.text: Apply contact precautions only
choices.label: B

choices.text: Ask visitors to wear gloves when entering the room
choices.label: C

choices.text: Place the client in a negative-pressure room
choices.label: D

items.scenarioText: The client has a chronic cough, weight loss, and a positive acid-fast bacillus smear.

distractorRationale.A: A client with active tuberculosis should not share a room because airborne transmission risk is high.
distractorRationale.B: Contact precautions alone do not address airborne spread.
distractorRationale.C: Gloves are not the key isolation measure for airborne TB exposure.

items.stem: A nurse is caring for a postoperative client who suddenly becomes restless, reports chest pain, and has an oxygen saturation of 88% on room air.
items.sourceReferenceTitle: Priority response to acute postoperative deterioration
items.explanation: Applying oxygen is an immediate action to support oxygenation while the nurse rapidly escalates care and continues assessment.
items.jurisdictionNotes: US acute care prioritization standards using ABCs.
items.rationale: Restlessness, chest pain, and hypoxemia suggest acute cardiopulmonary compromise. The nurse should address breathing and oxygenation first.
items.leadInQuestion: Which action should the nurse implement first?
learningObjectives: Use ABC prioritization during acute deterioration

choices.text: Document the findings in the electronic record
choices.label: A

choices.text: Apply oxygen via nasal cannula
choices.label: B

choices.text: Assist the client to ambulate in the hallway
choices.label: C

choices.text: Give the scheduled oral pain medication
choices.label: D

items.scenarioText: The client is 12 hours postoperative after abdominal surgery and was stable 30 minutes ago.

distractorRationale.A: Documentation is important but follows immediate intervention for an unstable client.
distractorRationale.C: Ambulation is unsafe during acute chest pain and hypoxemia.
distractorRationale.D: Oral medication does not address the urgent oxygenation problem.
